findings.passage: “We support reasonable steps that help maintain trust in our elections, including the voter identification requirements we already have in Virginia,” said the senators. “But the SAVE America Act goes far beyond that – it is a pretext for voter suppression.
findings.note: Joint statement issued by Warner and Kaine on the SAVE America Act ahead of a Senate vote. Says they support the existing Virginia voter ID requirements and opposes the bill's added requirements.

findings.passage: Republicans continue to raise baseless fears about election fraud and noncitizen voting, despite the fact that our elections are regularly audited and have also been tested repeatedly in courts, especially after 2020. Yet, no evidence of widespread voter fraud has ever been found.
findings.note: Same joint statement. Addresses claims of election fraud and non-citizen voting.

findings.passage: However, 40 percent of all Virginians — or nearly 3.3 million people — lack a valid passport, and almost 2 million women in Virginia may not have a birth certificate that matches their current legal name.
findings.note: Same press release, issued in the senators' names. Describes how many Virginians lack a passport or a matching birth certificate, the documents the bill would accept as proof of citizenship.

findings.passage: Under the SAVE America Act, voters would be required to provide proof of citizenship – such as a passport or birth certificate – to register to vote and photo identification to cast a ballot – even when voting by mail.
findings.note: Same press release. Describes the bill as requiring proof of citizenship to register and photo ID to vote, including by mail.

findings.passage: “Similarly, unsubstantiated claims by DOJ leadership of ‘tens of thousands noncitizens on voter rolls’ are reckless, as time and again, those claims have been refuted by findings that many individuals are falsely identified as noncitizens, and the extremely rare appearance of noncitizen registrants on the voter rolls or the even more extremely rare cases of noncitizen voters are often due to bureaucratic errors or misunderstandings about eligibility, as opposed to intentional fraud.”
findings.note: Passage from a letter to the Acting Attorney General signed by Warner, quoted in the press release. Covers claims of non-citizens on voter rolls and Justice Department voter-roll lawsuits.

findings.passage: “Given the time-sensitive nature of these claims, and the potential for misuse of this information for political purposes in the upcoming 2026 midterm elections, please provide weekly updates on the status of your investigation to the leadership of the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Government Affairs, and Senate Committee on the Judiciary,” the senators concluded.
findings.note: Letter signed by Warner asking the DHS inspector general to investigate federal officers' access to Virginia voter registration records. Related to voter-roll checks, not ID rules directly.

findings.passage: The executive order, which has been challenged in the courts, would direct the United States Postal Service (USPS) to create and maintain “Mail-in Absentee Participations Lists” that would determine which voters are eligible to receive and cast absentee ballots through the mail.
findings.note: Press release on a letter Warner joined opposing an executive order on mail ballots and postal lists of eligible voters. Related to who may receive a mail ballot; no ID rule is named. Release text, not a direct quote of Warner.

findings.note: Warner is recorded as Nay on the Senate roll call.
